text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: P1 auth-proxy: sudden spike in 401s from multiple regions, possible credential replay. oncall: @alex paged
alex: on it, joining bridge (callsign: alex-sre). any known deploys?
meera: no deploys flagged. I pulled a 5m sample, looks like repeated malformed Authorization headers containing partial token fragments.
ivan: can you paste the query you ran?
meera: `grpc_logs | where service=="auth-proxy" and status==401 | parse header as token_fragment | stats count() by src_ip, token_fragment | sort -count`
alex: seeing same. top src_ip clusters from two cloud providers, traffic pattern looks automated (high qps, varied UA).
kai: could be credential stuffing or a leaked token being replayed. any sign of token reuse across tenants?
meera: token fragments map to multiple tenant ids in logs — bad. sampling shows one fragment lines up with a key used by svc-ingest in staging logs bucket last night.
ivan: staging bucket? which one? we need immediate containment.
meera: s3://redwood-staging-logs-processed, object path /2026-03-17/ingest/*.gz — found plaintext Authorization header in a few gz files.
alex: ok escalate: WAF rule to block the top 20 offending IPs + rate-limit auth-proxy path. @ivan can you deploy a temporary ipset+waf rule?
ivan: deploying ipset now, rule id waf-temp-17678. applying rate-limit 30r/s per ip to /v1/generate endpoints. rolling out in us-west-2 -> meera confirm traffic drop.
meera: after apply, 401 spike drops ~85% in us-west, still see low-level retries from other regions. good stopgap.
kai: we should rotate any keys that appear in those files. which service accounts?
meera: svc-ingest-api and svc-debug-runner keys found in plaintext. both are staging creds but svc-ingest has access keys that can cross to prod via assume-role.
alex: assume-role path exists. immediate action: (1) rotate those two IAM access keys, (2) add deny policy to the assume-role for the old key ARN, (3) revoke active sessions for tokens derived from those keys. @kai take lead on rotation.
kai: starting rotation: creating new access keys, swapping credentials in staging tasks, marking old keys Inactive. will coordinate with deploy pipeline to pick up new creds. ETA 12m.
ivan: request to infra: can we suspend cross-account assume-role until keys rotated?
alex: yes, adding a temporary deny-based SCP for the role for 15m. doing that now.
meera: capturing evidence for incident doc: sample paths and object ids, redacted screenshots attached to ticket.
legal: tagging in legal. probable PII exposure? staging logs include user identifiers and partial ids. need to start data-exposure checklist and customer notice assessment.
legal: start collecting scope — which tenants impacted, timeframe, retention. please DM me the list and attach ticket.
alex: ops note: created bridge #incident-1767804321, created ticket INC-17678, I’ll hand to postmortem after containment.
ivan: WAF rule applied, ipset block shows drop, rate-limit in place. forwarding blocked ip list to netsec.
kai: rotated keys, old keys set to Inactive and scheduled Delete in 7 days, swapped creds in staging tasks and restarted workers. monitoring for rollbacks.
meera: confirm: no evidence of prod access using those keys after timestamp 1767780000. safe to reopen assume-role in 30m once no anomalies.
alex: good. next steps: complete key rotation audit, clean leaked logs from staging S3 (run secure delete), update pipeline to scrub auth headers before storage, legal to advise on external notification.
legal: will join post-rotation call in 20m to confirm notification plan.
pagerbot: incident status update: P1 -> contained (temporary mitigations applied). tracking oncall: alex, followup owner: meera.
alex: thanks team. final: keep monitoring for 2 hours, keep the bridge open for updates. :thumbsup:
